design: MemoryConsolidationService.consolidate implements MemoryConsolidationPort for the closed OpenAPI MemoryConsolidationRequest (GovernedEnvelope + input_query_digest, input_item_refs, algorithm_ref/digest, target kind/scope, reviewer_policy_ref; unevaluated properties refused). The MemoryConsolidationJob (LLD v1.1 §2.8.5) binds operation, tenant, the caller isolation tuple without the per-request correlation id, input query digest, exact input refs and item digests, algorithm/model pins, profile, target kind/scope, reviewer policy and budget; its digest is the job identity, its ref the derived items' source_ref.

Only approved ConsolidationProfiles run: an implemented, pinned algorithm (claim-merge 1.0; algorithm_digest = digest of its specification), target kinds within EPISODIC/SEMANTIC/REFLECTION, reviewer policies mapping to PROPOSED or (only for profiles approved as automatic) ACTIVE, retention policy and input-count/byte budgets. PROCEDURAL, WORKING, PREFERENCE, DISSENT and TEAM_SHARED are never consolidation targets.

Inputs are resolved from the memory ledger and must be visible to the caller (tenant, organization, domain, purpose equal; compartments included; marking dominated) or the request fails with the same MEMORY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND problem as an unknown ref; then they must be the current, ACTIVE, valid head (else LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_INVALID, MEMORY_TAINTED for QUARANTINED, POLICY_DENIED for expired). The live ConsolidationPolicy decision (bundle-bound) is taken before any content is read; content is read through the store coordinator and re-bound to the admitted item and content digests.

claim-merge groups the inputs' assertions by (subject, attribute): one canonical value becomes a statement citing every supporting version; several values become an UNRESOLVED conflict keeping every alternative and its supporting versions, ordered by canonical value bytes and never by support, and one separate DISSENT item per conflict (consolidates_refs = exactly the conflicting inputs). The derived item (new id bound to the job digest) cites every input by version ref, item digest and content digest, records the conflicts with their dissent refs and an uncertainty record (uncertainty_ref = its digest), has confidence floor6(min input confidence x statements/(statements+conflicts)), the union of the input taint plus DERIVED (and MODEL_GENERATED for REFLECTION), the conservative marking join, the shared scope owner, valid_until = earliest input valid_until, instruction_eligible false.

MemoryConsolidationService.correct corrects agreed statements of the current consolidated version by version n+1 (supersedes_ref and correction_of_ref = version n) carrying the same sources, conflicts, dissent refs and lineage; a correction touching a conflict key (DISSENT_ERASURE), citing anything outside the corrected version's sources (CORRECTION_SOURCE_REWRITE) or targeting a DISSENT item (DISSENT_IMMUTABLE) is refused. ConsolidationGuardPolicy wraps the admission policy: MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION items, new versions of consolidation-derived items and content rewrites of DISSENT items are permitted only for the exact item digest the service registered for the admission in progress.

Every derived item goes through the real admission service (closed schema, lineage, taint, marking, provenance resolved through ConsolidationReferenceResolver: the job/correction source and a provenance record covering it and every input evidence ref) and the real store coordinator. Completion order: derived items admitted and committed, success audit event recorded, then the job record appended; the receipt (OpenAPI OperationReceipt, audit_ref = digest of the audit event) exists only after both. Jobs are idempotent per (tenant, operation_id): a replay returns the recorded outcome (also after inputs were superseded), another job or operation kind conflicts, and a retry after a partial failure completes the same derived slots. The JournalConsolidationJobLedger is hash-chained, fsync'ed and flock-serialised.

Denials are audited (reason, detail, operation, GCS digest, binding, correlation, never payload content); an unaudited denial fails closed (AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE). Metrics use the bounded label set operation kind x {COMPLETED, REPLAYED, DENIED} x closed reason code.

inputs_tree_definition: git rev-parse <commit>:inputs (tree della directory inputs/ immutabile)
normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 Part II §2.9 'Frequency or majority does not erase dissent' is applied strictly: a disagreement never yields a statement, whatever the support counts; the alternatives' order is by value so that position carries no majority signal. Resolving a conflict is not a correction: it needs a separate record (LLD v1.1 §2.8 'Dissent non può essere sovrascritto: la risoluzione crea un record separato'), which this task does not create.

input_query_digest is recorded and pinned in the job digest as the selection query identity; the selection actually consolidated is bound separately by the exact input refs and item digests (input_selection_digest). The service does not re-execute the query.

The job budget of LLD v1.1 §2.8.5 is carried by the approved profile (the OpenAPI request has no budget field) and recorded in the job; exceeding it is POLICY_DENIED/CONSOLIDATION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED (quota behaviour, never semantic downgrade, ADD §2.13).

Consolidation inputs must be visible under the caller's own isolation tuple with an identical purpose; cross-project/federated consolidation would need its own approved Authority profile and is not opened here. The target scope owner is taken from the inputs and must be shared by all of them.
Lifecycle status of outputs comes from the reviewer policy of the profile: ACTIVE only for profiles approved as automatic, PROPOSED otherwise; a correction keeps the status of the corrected version.
raw_output_format: JSONL: una riga per comando/artefatto/osservazione con label, command, exit_code, sha256 dei byte UTF-8 archiviati e output integrale; le credenziali locali generate (valori di .ocor/bootstrap.env) sono sostituite da <redacted:NAME> prima dell'archiviazione e dell'hash, gli originali restano solo fuori da Git; DSN mostrato come <local generated credential>

requirement_results.command: FGM-03 on real PostgreSQL (metadata, encrypted content, full-text), Qdrant and OpenBao transit: WORKING run memory consolidates into a NEW EPISODIC and a NEW SEMANTIC item (MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION, consolidates_refs = the exact input versions, derived_from_refs, job ref/digest as source, uncertainty record bound by uncertainty_ref, confidence never above the weakest input, union taint, conservative marking join, scope owner shared by every input); the payload cites every input by version ref, item digest and content digest; every input keeps its item digest, its stored bytes and its head; a reviewed profile yields PROPOSED outputs only; the request and receipt follow the OpenAPI MemoryConsolidationRequest/OperationReceipt

FGM-13 on the real backends: five reports 'open' against one 'closed' produce no statement for that key but an UNRESOLVED conflict keeping both alternatives with their own supporting versions, ordered by value and never by support, a separate DISSENT item (MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION, consolidates_refs = exactly the conflicting inputs) cited by the summary in derived_from_refs and conflicts[].dissent_ref, and a confidence reduced by the conflict; three-way and tied disagreements keep every alternative; agreed keys still become statements citing every supporting version

FGM-09 on the real backends: a correction of an agreed statement is version 2 of the consolidated item (supersedes_ref and correction_of_ref = version 1), with the same consolidates/derived_from lineage, the same cited sources and the same conflicts and dissent refs; version 1, every source and every DISSENT item keep their item digest, stored bytes and head; the correction envelope is closed

on the real backends: a correction that resolves either side of a conflict (DISSENT_ERASURE), cites a source outside the corrected version or an invented one (CORRECTION_SOURCE_REWRITE), targets a DISSENT item (DISSENT_IMMUTABLE), a plain memory item, an unknown or a superseded version, or is denied/unauthorized is refused, audited and writes nothing; a correction, a DISSENT content rewrite or a fabricated consolidation item submitted through plain admission is denied by the consolidation guard; REFLECTION output carries MODEL_GENERATED and is never instruction-eligible; no output is ever instruction-eligible and the module has no canonical, approval, lease, action or promotion path

only approved profiles run (unknown algorithm, drifted algorithm digest, unapproved reviewer policy, unapproved or never-consolidated target kind such as PROCEDURAL/WORKING/DISSENT are refused); policy denial, outage, stale bundle and invalid decisions fail closed before any content read; input-count and byte budgets, an elapsed or elapsing deadline and unparseable inputs refuse before any write; every denial is audited with correlation and without payload content, and an unaudited denial fails closed; metrics use a bounded label set

on the real backends: inputs of another tenant, organization, domain or purpose, outside the caller compartments or above its marking are refused with exactly the same problem as unknown versions, before any policy call or content read; superseded, revoked, quarantined, proposed, expired or uncommitted inputs are refused; a target scope owner not shared by every input is refused

duplicate delivery and failure injection on the real backends: a replay (other deadline or correlation id, even after an input was superseded) returns the recorded outcome without writing; the same operation with another job or operation kind conflicts; outcomes persist across runs in the hash-chained job journal over fresh adapters, and a tampered or torn journal fails closed; a content-store failure after the dissent write, an audit outage or a job-ledger outage return no receipt and the retry completes the same derived slots without duplicates; a derived slot squatted by another item is never adopted (DERIVED_SLOT_OCCUPIED); a dropped or re-digested journal entry fails closed

residual_risks: claim-merge is a deterministic structural algorithm over explicit (subject, attribute, value) assertions; no model-generated summarisation is implemented or claimed. REFLECTION output of this task is the same structural merge, tainted MODEL_GENERATED by rule.

Dissent resolution records, lifecycle transitions of derived items and their deletion cascade are not part of this task (OCOR-DEV-0055/0056); the guard denies new admitted versions of DISSENT items that change content but lifecycle versions appended by the coordinator are outside its path.
The ConsolidationReferenceResolver registry of job/correction provenance is in-process; a cross-run retry re-registers it before any new admission and replays need no resolution.
The PostgreSQL/Qdrant/OpenBao adapters are the 0051 test adapters; no production adapter under memory/adapters/ exists yet.

tdd.REFACTOR: First live run exposed one wrong test oracle (a marking below the caller context cannot be admitted, so the marking-join case now admits the lower input under an UNCLASSIFIED context and adds the negative and positive UNCLASSIFIED-caller cases). Before the first run the service was restructured so that a replay is answered before the currency checks of inputs and correction targets (an operation stays replayable after its inputs or target were superseded) and the job ledger outage is mapped to a closed problem. A preliminary mutation probe left seven survivors: two were redundant code and were removed (a deadline re-check identical to the admission service's own deadline check at the first derived admission; an operation-kind comparison implied by the job digest, which covers different closed structures for consolidation and correction); one was an equivalent mutant replaced by a meaningful one (the marking join equals the context marking because every input is dominated by the context; the mutant now takes one input's marking and is refused by admission as MARKING_DOWNGRADE); four exposed missing tests, now added (content rewrite of a directly admitted DISSENT item, a squatted derived slot never adopted, journal chain and entry digest verified separately).
